topPRs.title: op-service: move PathFlag to a leaf package so oppprof is importable downstream
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
## What

Moves `PathFlag` out of `op-service/flags` into a new leaf package `op-service/cliflags`, and adds a `depguard` test that keeps the consumer-facing half of `op-service` free of the superchain config bundle.

A rename, a two-line import swap in `op-service/oppprof/cli.go`, and a guard test (plus the `depguard` helper it needs).

## The bug

`op-service/oppprof` needs exactly one thing from `op-service/flags`: the `PathFlag` value type, for `--pprof.path`. Two references.

But `op-service/flags` also defines the `--network` flag, whose **usage string** interpolates the network list:

```go
Usage: fmt.Sprintf("Predefined network selection. Available networks: %s",
    strings.Join(chaincfg.AvailableNetworks(), ", ")),
```

Go compiles at package granularity, so that one help-string reference puts `op-node/chaincfg` — and with it `op-core/superchain` and its embedded `superchain-configs.zip` — into the build closure of every consumer of a pprof flag.

`superchain-configs.zip` is generated by `sync-superchain.sh` and gitignored, so it is **absent from the published module**. Anything reaching `op-core/superchain` therefore cannot be built by a downstream consumer at all:

```
op-core/superchain/chain.go:21:12: pattern superchain-configs.zip: no matching files found
```

So `op-service/oppprof` — and any service wiring up pprof flags — has been unimportable outside this repo since the registry moved into `op-core`. Before that, the data came from op-geth's own `superchain` package, which ships intact, so a downstream op-geth `replace` covered it. It no longer does.

Being precise about the mechanism: making the usage string lazy would *not* fix this. The `import` is what pulls the bundle in, whether or not the function is called. The package boundary has to move.

## How it was found

Bumping a downstream service ([infrastructure-services#1358](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infrastructure-services/pull/1358)) hit this and had to pin `optimism v1.19.0`, the last version that builds for a consumer reaching `oppprof`:

| optimism version | `go build op-service/oppprof` from a bare consumer module |
|---|---|
| v1.18.0 | builds |
| v1.19.0 | builds |
| v1.19.1 / v1.19.2 / v1.19.5 | missing `superchain-configs.zip` |

## The fix

`PathFlag` moves verbatim to `op-service/cliflags`, which imports only the standard library. `op-service/flags` keeps the chain-selection flags and its `chaincfg` dependency, which is legitimate — it is *about* chain selection.

After the move, every commonly-consumed `op-service` package is bundle-free:

```
clean   cliapp  cliflags  client  ctxinterrupt  eth  httputil  ioutil
        jsonutil  log  metrics  oppprof  rpc  signer  tls  txmgr
BUNDLE  flags          ← correct and intended
```

`oppprof` was the only leak.

## The guard

`op-service/deps_test.go` guards **all 76 packages** under `op-service/...` against a transitive `op-core/superchain` import, using a new `depguard.RequireNoTransitiveImportExcept`. It is an allowlist rather than a list of guarded packages, so the invariant holds by default and a newly added package is covered automatically.

The allowlist is checked in **both** directions: an entry that no longer reaches a forbidden import fails too, so entries cannot outlive the dependency that justified them.

**Both failure modes are covered by positive controls** in `depguard_test.go`, and the `op-service` guard was confirmed to fail on the pre-fix code:

```
--- FAIL: TestOpServiceIsImportableDownstream
    op-service/oppprof -> op-service/flags -> op-node/chaincfg -> op-core/superchain
```

It runs in the existing Go test job — no new CI job needed.

### The allowlist documents a second, unfixed root

Enumerating the exceptions showed `op-service/flags` is not the only way in. Seven of the eight come from `op-core/interop/depset`, whose `FromRegistry` loader sits in the same package as the `DependencySet` types:

```
op-service/{apis,dial,sources,testutils,txintent,...} -> op-core/interop/depset -> op-core/superchain
```

`sources` and `apis` use only the *types*, never `FromRegistry` — the same shape as the `PathFlag` problem, and it would yield to the same split. That matters: `op-service/sources` is the OP-aware eth client, which downstream repos import (proxyd does), so they cannot build against a current monorepo either. Left out of this PR to keep it reviewable, recorded against each allowlist entry.

## Verification

- With `superchain-configs.zip` deleted (reproducing the published-module condition), `go build ./op-service/oppprof` fails before this change and succeeds after.
- A throwaway external module importing `op-service/oppprof` and `op-service/cliflags`, with the bundle absent, builds against this tree.
- `go build ./...` passes across the repo; `op-service`, `op-node/rollup` and the touched packages' tests pass; `gofmt` clean.

## Naming

`op-service/cliflags` holds custom `urfave/cli` value types, sitting alongside `cliiface`/`cliapp`, with a doc comment stating the leaf constraint.

It is close in name to `op-service/flags`, which I'm not thrilled about. The cleaner fix is arguably to rename the *other* package — `op-service/flags` is really superchain/chain-selection flags (`--network`, `--rollup.config`, fork overrides), and a name saying so would make the split self-explaining and leave the generic name free. That's a wider rename (7 importers) so I've kept it out of this PR, but happy to do it here or as a follow-up if you'd prefer.

## Related

Context in [cloud-security#324](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/cloud-security/issues/324) and `docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md` §20 (added in #22664), which records downstream consumers as a class of blocker for the op-geth decoupling.
